narrative.overview:
MSITest is a flight deck for test operations. Every instrument reads clearly at a glance. Status lights tell the story before you read a word. The layout is dense where it needs to be (run tables, step timelines, console output) and breathes where density would hurt (section separators, card interiors, settings forms). Nothing is decorative. Everything is reachable.

The system draws from Airtable's visual language: a single saturated blue as the structural accent, generous border radii that soften without rounding into playfulness, and a strict division between the system font stack (body, labels, headings) and monospace (all technical content). The sidebar is the flight deck's instrument panel: always present, always blue, carrying navigation and status counts.

This system explicitly rejects AI-adjacent visual cliches. No sparkle icons, no gradient text, no purple or violet accents, no chatbot-style response cards. When AI analysis appears, it reads like a senior engineer's comment in a pull request: plain text, inline code snippets, a confidence percentage. The AI is infrastructure, not identity.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained color: one saturated blue (Anchor Blue) carries navigation, primary actions, and active states
Generous radii (12/16px) on all interactive elements and containers
Monospace for all technical content: test names, IDs, durations, file paths, code, status labels
Status is always visible via color-coded pills with dot indicators
Flat surfaces by default with blue-tinted elevation on raised elements

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Anchor Blue is the only saturated color used for UI chrome. Semantic colors (success, warn, danger) appear exclusively in status indicators and trend arrows. No other hue family enters the interface.

rules.name: The Blue-Tint Shadow Rule
rules.body: All elevation shadows carry a blue component (rgba(45, 127, 249, 0.28)). Neutral-gray shadows look dead. The blue tint ties raised elements to the accent system.

rules.name: The Code Boundary Rule
rules.body: If the user might select it, copy it, or grep for it, it must be monospace. Test names, file paths, durations, status labels, console output, code snippets. Body text is for prose. Mono is for data.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Elevation is earned, not assumed. If a card or section does not need to float above its context, it should not have a shadow. Border color alone separates most elements.

dos: Do use monospace for any content a developer might copy, grep, or reference in a terminal: test names, file paths, IDs, durations, console output, code snippets, status labels.
Do surface status immediately with color-coded pills and dot indicators. Pass/fail/flaky/running should read without scanning.
Do use Anchor Blue for exactly three things: navigation chrome (sidebar), primary actions (buttons), and active/focus states.
Do use the blue-tinted raised shadow for settings sections and onboarding cards.
Do give every interactive element a focus-visible state: the 3px blue ring at 70% transparency.
donts: Don't use sparkle icons, magic wand imagery, gradient text, chatbot-style response cards, or any visual language that signals "AI tool."
Don't introduce a second saturated accent color. One accent (Anchor Blue) owns the interface.
Don't use pure black (#000) for text. Ink (#181d26) carries a blue undertone.
Don't add shadows to table rows, stat cards, filter bars, or list items. Flat with borders.
Don't use display fonts in UI labels, buttons, data cells, or status indicators.
Don't animate layout properties. Transitions on background-color, border-color, box-shadow, opacity, transform only. 150-200ms.
Don't make the interface feel playful, whimsical, or personality-forward.
